```{python}
#| label: fig-hw-sweep
#| fig-cap: "One full sweep of the valid space, software against the device. The software loop finishes in 1.92 us and the device needs 80 us at 140 MHz, so throughput belongs to the CPU and not to this hardware. The figure is here to stop the decode rate being read as a speed claim."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

points = 11172
sw_us = 1.92
hw_140_us = points / 140e6 * 1e6
hw_12_us = points / 12e6 * 1e6

labels = ['software loop\n(11,172 to_axes)', 'device at 140 MHz', 'device at 12 MHz']
us = [sw_us, hw_140_us, hw_12_us]
x = np.arange(len(labels))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.4, 3.6))

ax.bar(x, us, 0.5, color='white', edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.8, hatch='///')
ax.set_yscale('log')
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=8.5)
ax.set_ylabel('time for one sweep (us, log)', fontsize=9)
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle=':', alpha=0.3, which='both')

for xi, v in enumerate(us):
    ax.text(xi, v * 1.45, f'{v:.2f} us', fontsize=8.5, ha='center')

ax.annotate('', xy=(1, hw_140_us), xytext=(0, sw_us),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='dimgray', lw=1.0))
ax.text(0.5, sw_us * 2.6, f'{hw_140_us / sw_us:.0f}x slower', fontsize=8,
        ha='center', color='dimgray')

plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```
